newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss govt sees weak economic recovery in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Swiss govt sees weak economic recovery in 1997.

text.p: The Swiss government said on Wednesday it expected a weak economic upturn in 1997 after six consecutive years of stagnation.

"The economic outlook for 1997 is somewhat better given the business cycle upturn in western Europe and improvements in price competitiveness resulting from the most recent weakening of the Swiss franc's foreign exchange rate," the cabinet said.
"But the economy will recover only hesitantly," it added in a statement, noting Europe's economic revival was only modest and there were few signs for now of an imminent export boom.
The statement, issued after the cabinet accepted the economics ministry's 1996 report on international economic policy, did not give a precise forecast for 1997 growth.
The 1997 federal budget is based on real GDP growth of 1.5 percent, well above the 0.5 percent forecasts from the official Commission for Economic Policy and the Swiss National Bank.
Estimates for 1996 put the GDP drop at around 0.5 to 0.7 percent after scant growth of 0.1 percent in 1995.
